The `sha256sums` array uses 'SKIP', which is expected and acceptable for VCS packages where checksums cannot be predetermined. The `pkgver()` function dynamically computes the version from Git metadata, a common pattern in `-git` packages.

No suspicious or malicious operations are present. There are no network requests outside the declared source, no use of `eval`, no obfuscated code, and no unexpected file or system modifications. The build process only invokes standard Autotools commands on the locally checked-out source. The package depends only on standard GNOME and build system components. All actions are consistent with the declared purpose: building and installing a GNOME Shell extension from its upstream Git repository.

While the source is not pinned to a specific commit (it will track HEAD), this is normal for `-git` packages and not inherently malicious. The lack of a pinned source affects reproducibility but does not introduce active malicious behavior. No evidence of supply-chain attacks or injected code is found.
</details>
